result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both use a monospace stack at about 14px with comfortable line-height. Both keep the timestamp, level and service in fixed columns and wrap long messages at roughly 95-100 characters, not at prose width. A edges ahead for quick scanning because of its filled level badges, column headers and denser rows, though its header labels sit slightly left of the data columns; B's colored-text levels are clear but lighter, and its long stack traces take up much more vertical space. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both use monospace text at about 14px with roughly 1.5 line-height, wrap long messages in a wide column of about 100 characters, and line up timestamp, level and service in fixed columns. B has column headers, solid badge-style level labels (ERROR stands out a lot) and filter chips, so it's quicker to scan. A also works but marks levels only with small colored text, so they're less distinct.
